entities.summary:
Pedro Nuño Colón de Portugal y Castro, 6th Duke of Veragua, 6th Marquess of Jamaica, and 6th Count of Gelves, a direct descendant of Christopher Columbus, held the prestigious but tragically brief office of Viceroy of New Spain from December 3 to December 8, 1673. Born in Madrid in 1618, his appointment by King Charles II of Spain represented the enduring recognition of the Columbus lineage and its historical claims to territories in the Americas. His journey across the Atlantic to assume the highest administrative post in the most significant viceroyalty of the Spanish Empire was a monumental undertaking, symbolizing the vast reach of imperial power and the personal sacrifices demanded of its administrators in the Early Modern era.

Upon his arrival in Veracruz in October 1673, after a long and arduous sea voyage, the Duke immediately fell ill. Despite his deteriorating health, he pressed on to Mexico City, where he formally took possession of his office on December 3, 1673. His tenure as viceroy, however, lasted a mere five days. He succumbed to his illness, likely exacerbated by the rigors of travel and the change in climate, dying on December 8, 1673, before he could implement a single policy or issue any significant decree. This abrupt end to his viceroyalty left the nascent colonial administration in a state of immediate transition, requiring the rapid appointment of an interim successor.
